title: Complex Conformal Manifolds
abstract: Constructs complex CFTs by analytic continuation of exactly marginal couplings and argues genuinely complex RATIONAL CFTs do not exist -- rational points are confined to the real regime -- with verification against non-Hermitian critical lattice systems.
key_claims: Complex CFTs can be constructed by analytically continuing exactly marginal couplings into the complex plane.
Claims genuinely complex rational CFTs do not exist: rational points on conformal manifolds are confined to the real regime.
Verified against non-Hermitian critical systems, mapping the landscape of complex fixed points (5-state-Potts-type walking RG scenarios).
relevance_note: WATCH. Landscape context for the non-Hermitian/complex-CFT side of HYP-028. Important scoping fact: Yang-Lee M(2,5) is a REAL non-unitary rational CFT, so the no-complex-rational-CFT claim constrains the complex-CFT (5-state-Potts-type) sector, NOT the M(2,5) target of HYP-028. No routing required; keep as boundary-of-landscape reference if the non-Hermitian program ever drifts toward complex fixed points.
anchor_contradiction: None. Does not touch alpha=4, transport, or the ED-inaccessibility finding; constrains a different (complex-rational) sector than the real non-unitary M(2,5) target.
